limitations_and_boundaries: The study uses 2D in vitro cultures; 3D in vivo validation is not provided.
Rescue experiments (e.g., restoring actomyosin contractility after inhibition) were not performed.
The causal link between fibronectin secretion and leader-cell formation is inferred from correlation and cycloheximide inhibition, not direct genetic perturbation.
The selected source chunks do not report a rescue, reconstitution, reversal, or epistasis experiment; that rung of the causal evidence chain remains untested within this extraction scope.

research_questions.statement: Does compressive stress stimulate migration of mammary carcinoma cells and what are the underlying mechanisms?

provenance.text_excerpt: These results demonstrate that applied compressive stress (ACS) enhances the migration potential of mammary carcinoma cells independent of any changes in cell proliferation.

claims.statement: Applied compressive stress enhances the migration potential of mammary carcinoma cells independent of changes in cell proliferation.

experiments_or_tasks: Assessed cell morphology and cytoskeletal organization at wound edge using phalloidin staining for F-actin and anti-tubulin antibodies.

Subjected five mammary epithelial cell lines (MCF10A, MCF7, 67NR, 4T1, MDA-MB-231) to constant compressive stress of 5.8 mmHg using a weighted piston and measured migration rates via scratch-wound assay.

methods.name: In vitro compression device and scratch-wound assay
methods.protocol_description: Cells were subjected to 16-h compressive stress at 5.8 mmHg using a weighted piston pressing against a membrane surface. Migration was measured via scratch-wound assay. Cell lines: MCF10A, MCF7, 67NR, 4T1, MDA-MB-231.

study_units.name: Compression-induced migration and cytoskeletal remodeling

provenance.text_excerpt: compressed 67NR cells showed actin stress fiber alignment and microtubule rearrangement

results.value_raw_text: Compressed 67NR cells showed actin stress fiber alignment and microtubule rearrangement at the wound edge.

provenance.text_excerpt: compressive stress did enhance the motility of highly aggressive 4T1 and MDA-MB-231 cells, as well as 67NR cells... In contrast, compressive stress suppressed the migration of normal mammary epithelial MCF10A and non-invasive, well-differentiated MCF7 cells

results.value_raw_text: Compressive stress enhanced motility of 4T1, MDA-MB-231, and 67NR cells, but suppressed migration of MCF10A and MCF7 cells.

provenance.text_excerpt: compression can initiate directional protrusions for leader-cell formation independent of actomyosin contractility; however, the contractile machinery is still necessary for sheet migration.

claims.statement: Compression can initiate leader-cell formation independent of actomyosin contractility, but contractile machinery is necessary for sheet migration.

experiments_or_tasks: Measured wound closure rates and leader-cell formation under compression.
Used dominant-negative RhoA (RhoA-T19N) retrovirus, ROCK inhibitor Y-27632, MLCK inhibitor ML-7, and myosin II ATPase inhibitor Blebbistatin to alter actomyosin contractility.

methods.name: Pharmacological and molecular inhibition of actomyosin contractility
methods.protocol_description: 67NR cells were transduced with dominant-negative RhoA-T19N retrovirus or treated with Y-27632 (5 or 30 μM), ML-7 (25 μM), or Blebbistatin (50 μM). Wound closure rates and leader-cell formation were assessed under control or compressed (5.8 mmHg) conditions for 16 h.

study_units.name: Role of actomyosin contractility in leader-cell formation and migration

provenance.text_excerpt: Similar results were seen with Y-27632 and ML-7 treatment

results.value_raw_text: Y-27632 and ML-7 treatment did not suppress leader-cell formation in compressed cultures.

provenance.text_excerpt: Compression still enhanced wound closure rates of RhoT19N cells compared with uncompressed controls, but the effect was slightly reduced compared with the induction seen in wild-type cells.

results.value_raw_text: Compression still enhanced wound closure rates of RhoT19N cells compared with uncompressed controls, but effect slightly reduced compared to wild-type.

provenance.text_excerpt: when actomyosin contractility was completely blocked by the myosin II ATPase inhibitor Blebbistatin, compressive stress was still able to induce leader-cell formation despite compromised cell motility

experiments_or_tasks: Patterned 67NR cells into circles, rosettes, and squares using microcontact printing to control free-cell perimeter.
Quantified leader-cell formation and migration speed under control and compressed conditions.

methods.protocol_description: 67NR cells were patterned on fibronectin-stamped surfaces to form circles, rosettes, and squares. Leader-cell formation and migration speed were quantified from time-lapse images.

Inhibited protein synthesis with cycloheximide to assess fibronectin secretion.
Quantified cell-substrate adhesion using fluid shear detachment assay.

methods.name: Cell adhesion assay and fibronectin analysis
methods.protocol_description: Cell-substrate adhesion was quantified by exposing compressed or control 67NR cells to fluid shear and measuring remaining adherent cells via crystal violet stain (OD at 540 nm). Fibronectin distribution was assessed by immunofluorescence and quantitative PCR. Cycloheximide (1 μM) was used to inhibit protein translation.
